item.title: Kofukuji: The Five-Story Pagoda of Nara — Guide
item.description: Kofukuji, founded by the Fujiwara clan and moved to Nara in 710, was once among the most powerful temples in Japan, and its five-story pagoda — at 50 metres the second-tallest wooden pagoda in the country — is an icon of the city, rising beside Sarusawa Pond at the very entrance to Nara Park. Beyond the pagoda and the rebuilt Central Golden Hall, the temple’s greatest treasure is its National Treasure Museum, home to a celebrated collection of ancient Buddhist sculpture including the beloved three-faced, six-armed Ashura statue, one of Japan’s most admired religious artworks.

item.title: Tanzan Shrine: The Wooden Pagoda in the Autumn Hills — Guide
item.description: Tanzan Shrine, tucked into the wooded mountains south of Sakurai, is one of Nara’s most beautiful hidden gems, dedicated to Fujiwara no Kamatari, founder of the mighty Fujiwara clan, whose plot to reform the state was supposedly hatched on this mountain. Its treasure is unique: a graceful vermilion thirteen-story wooden pagoda, the only one of its kind surviving anywhere in the world, rising in tiers among the trees. The shrine is above all an autumn destination, when some 3,000 maple trees set the mountainside ablaze in reds and golds around the pagoda, one of the finest foliage sights in the Kansai region.

item.title: Iwate Events & Festivals: Chagu-Chagu Umakko, Sansa Odori & Hiraizumi Pageants
item.description: Iwate Prefecture Events and Festivals Guide for International Visitors Iwate Prefecture, Japan’s second-largest prefecture by area, offers visitors a rich tapestry of cultural festivals that showcase centuries-old traditions, stunning natural beauty, and the warm hospitality of the Tohoku region. From thunderous drum parades to sacred horse processions, these events provide unforgettable windows into northern Japan’s heritage. Chagu-Chagu Umakko: The Jingling Horse Parade When: Second Saturday of June (typically June 8-14)
